brief.instructions: Produce TWO distinct source-grounded hypotheses for improving our B200 deployment, no publication novelty gate. First investigate a decode-specific MegaMoE workspace for the active FlashInfer CuTeDSL backend using #62073: could lower address/capacity overhead improve decode while allocation steals KV cache? Require exact backend inclusion check, global capacity agreement, zero/unequal rank tests, DSpark verify token-bound contract. Second investigate transferring launch-time communication CTA/SM resource selection from paper2609.07536 to B200 shared-expert/combine overlap ONLY if active backend exposes a legal concurrency/resource knob. This is conditional mechanism transfer, not a claim A100 gains apply. Pre-dispatch quantization61962 is an alternative with severe scale-compatibility risk54683; do not invent a direct AMD-to-NVIDIA port. Avoid generic shape-switching GEMM proposal already in memory. Use source excerpts as author reports, concrete counterevidence, and compare to baseline R7b2xDEP4 at256/384/512 and R10DEP8 at1024 with controls. Baseline archive dspark_config=off conflicts refreshedk5; runtimeflags and image digest unknown and must be frozen before experiments. R7b customgoodput6.6288 vs AIPerf strict4.6727; reportboth. Novelty is irrelevant. No GPU execution now. All performance thresholds are proposed design choices.

experiment.control: Resolved deployed configuration plus the best legal fixed CTA/SM setting found on a tuning subset; include an overlap-disabled or early-join diagnostic where supported. Compare within R7b two DEP4 at 256/384/512 and R10 DEP8 at 1024.
experiment.correctness: Preserve collective order, stream/event dependencies, graph replay safety, and output equality or an agreed numerical tolerance. Do not infer a NVIDIA pre-dispatch quantization change from the AMD MoRI result; PR #54683 shows that scale semantics can forbid it.
experiment.cost: Read-only backend and knob inspection, then short profiling and bounded static tuning before paired eight-B200 serving tests. No GPU execution is available in this session.
experiment.held_out_condition: A held-out request trace with measured cache hits, different rank skew and concurrency from policy tuning, including zero and unequal rank work.
experiment.inconclusive_if: Backend state or runtime controls remain unknown, graph modes differ, traces cannot resolve overlap, or paired results are too noisy to distinguish the policy from the static comparator.
experiment.metrics: TTFT, TPOT/ITL, throughput, custom and AIPerf strict SLO goodput reported separately, cost per token, quality, combine and shared-expert timing, overlap interval, CTA residency, SM occupancy, and KV capacity.
experiment.rejects_if: No legal knob or overlap path exists, traces show no relevant contention, correctness fails, or the best fixed setting matches or beats the policy.
experiment.supports_if: A legal knob and resource contention are demonstrated, correctness passes, and paired full-serving results beat the best fixed setting on service metrics without material goodput, cost, KV, or quality regression.
experiment.treatment: A capture-compatible launch-time resource policy based on measured workload and residency constraints, using only documented legal settings.

card.statement: Investigate launch-time selection of communication CTA count or compute/communication SM resources for shared-expert and combine overlap on the B200 deployment. The cited paper describes such selection for COMET on four A100 GPUs and reports prefill gains; it explicitly leaves newer architectures and decode for future work. A separate DeepEP v2 report shows that shared-expert GEMMs can overlap combine in a GB300 deployment, but it does not establish a legal resource-selection knob in the active B200 backend. First inspect the resolved backend and profile whether combine and shared-expert work overlap or contend for resources. Only if a legal knob exists, compare a small, capture-compatible launch-time policy with the strongest fixed resource setting and the current serving baseline. B200 contention, decode benefit, and effect size remain unknown.

policy.baseline_comparison: Compare against the supplied R7b2xDEP4 results at 256/384/512 and R10DEP8 at 1024 under matched controls. The task reports R7b custom goodput of 6.6288 and AIPerf strict goodput of 4.6727; preserve both definitions. The historical source pin and refreshed configuration differ. Active engine, precision, backend, MTP/DSpark state, runtime flags, and image digest must be established before claiming a feature is absent or measuring a delta.

criteria.description: Required veto: identify a credible, testable path to task value and either a baseline delta or a cheap inspection that determines whether the feature is already active. Unknown bottlenecks may motivate an experiment.
criteria.justification: Both proposals can be useful even if their performance effects are currently unknown. Backend and configuration inspection is essential before estimating incremental value.

criteria.description: Required veto: show a correctness-preserving integration path. For the workspace, check active backend inclusion, global capacity agreement, zero and unequal rank cases, and the DSpark verify token-bound contract. For communication resource selection, establish that the active backend exposes a legal CTA/SM concurrency knob.
criteria.justification: These are the concrete failure modes and transfer preconditions in this task. Unknowns defer judgment; a demonstrated violation rejects the proposal.

criteria.description: Separate observed results, author claims, and B200 transfer inference; use exact short source passages and record unknown hardware, workload, effect size, and limitations.
criteria.justification: The supplied evidence is identifiers and titles, not source excerpts. A PR title or paper abstract cannot establish implementation behavior or B200 gains.

criteria.description: Specify matched baseline controls and measurements for TPOT, TTFT, throughput, cost per token, quality, and KV-cache capacity. Treat proposed performance thresholds as design choices.
criteria.justification: Workspace allocation may trade decode overhead against KV capacity; communication overlap may shift latency without improving end-to-end service value.

evidence.rationale: One substantive implementation source can support the workspace hypothesis; two independent citations are not a blanket requirement. The communication-transfer hypothesis additionally needs the cited paper’s full text and active-backend engineering evidence. These requirements are hypothesis-specific. Supplied titles alone satisfy neither.

policy.objective: Prioritize two testable B200 deployment hypotheses: a decode-specific MegaMoE workspace, and conditional transfer of communication CTA/SM resource selection to shared-expert/combine overlap. Seek useful improvement in TTFT, TPOT, throughput, cost per token, or quality without compromising correctness.
policy.rationale: Weights emphasize a useful baseline-relative path and legal, correct integration for these two specific mechanisms. The 70-point threshold is an uncalibrated prioritization choice, not an empirical cutoff; required vetoes apply independently, and unknown judgments defer rather than reject. The task explicitly says “No GPU execution in this session” and “75% target cacheability is not measured cache-hit rate.” No source results or author claims can be verified from the supplied titles, and no A100-to-B200 effect size is inferred.

legal_correct_integration.rationale: The proposed collective-order, stream-dependency, and graph-replay checks are appropriate, but no supplied evidence identifies the active B200 combine backend or establishes a legal CTA/SM resource knob. source_support.rationale: The supplied paper conclusion says it “selects the communication-CTA count and the compute/communication resource partition before kernel launch” and places its evaluation on four A100 GPUs; its future-work passage expressly leaves newer GPUs and decode untested. The excerpted paper text and PR do not provide active-backend engineering evidence or a legal knob.
